The event
Two days at UT Austin, Oct 22 to 23, building on the ScorePlay and Twelve Labs APIs to solve real content problems from Tottenham Hotspur and the San Antonio Spurs. Hosted by ScorePlay, Twelve Labs, The Players Fund, both clubs and the UT McCombs Business of Sports Institute.
The objective: show what teams can build when a club's media is open infrastructure and AI can understand it. Both clubs want tools they can put to work.
Format:
10 teams of up to 5
Thursday morning: onboarding and the brief
Thursday afternoon to Friday 2pm: build
Friday afternoon: presentations, judging and awards
The two building blocks
What's a MAM:
A media asset management platform is where an organization stores, organizes and distributes its photos and video
Every asset carries metadata: who's in it, the game, the date, rights, tags
Teams search it, pull from it, and push content out to social, broadcast, partners and sponsors
ScorePlay is the MAM here and the system of record
If it's not on the asset in ScorePlay, the club doesn't know it
Assets already carry player tags, so you can filter by who's in the shot
Starting point: think of the MAM as the source of truth you read from and write back to
What's video understanding:
Video understanding models "watch" video the way a person does, across visuals, audio, speech and on-screen text, and turn it into data you can search and use
Twelve Labs is the video understanding platform here. It has two models:
Marengo: search your footage in plain language ("dunk in transition") and find the exact moment
Pegasus: generate text from video, such as summaries, descriptions and tags
Starting point: think of Twelve Labs as the analyst that watches everything and hands you structured answers
How they fit together:
ScorePlay holds the content and knows who's in it
Twelve Labs understands what's happening in it
Your app connects the two
Example: filter ScorePlay for assets tagged with a player, then use Marengo to find the dunks in transition within those assets
